intro: New Hampshire's property taxes can make the difference between a home that appears affordable and one that stretches your monthly budget. Before choosing a property, consider the complete cost of financing, insurance, taxes and ongoing home maintenance.

Our free New Hampshire mortgage calculator estimates your monthly housing payment using your home price, down payment, interest rate and loan term. Whether you're buying in Manchester, Nashua, Concord, Portsmouth or a smaller Granite State community, use the calculator to compare financing arrangements before making an offer.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: How Much Is a Mortgage Payment in New Hampshire?

blocks.markdown:
A $400,000 New Hampshire home purchased with a 20% down payment and financed through a 30-year mortgage at a 6% fixed interest rate would have a monthly principal and interest payment of approximately $1,918.56.

sections.heading: Understanding the New Hampshire Housing Market

blocks.markdown:
New Hampshire offers housing opportunities across suburban communities, coastal neighborhoods, university towns and rural areas.

According to the [US Census Bureau's New Hampshire QuickFacts](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/NH), the median value of owner-occupied housing was $402,500 during the 2020–2024 survey period. Homeowners with mortgages reported median selected monthly ownership costs of $2,367, while the homeownership rate was 72.8%.

These historical figures include homeowners who purchased properties under different market conditions and interest rates.

Properties near the Massachusetts border or the Seacoast may have different purchase prices from homes in northern New Hampshire. Transportation, heating and maintenance expenses can also vary substantially between communities.

Research recent comparable sales in your preferred neighborhood before selecting a purchase price for the calculator.

sections.heading: How to Use the New Hampshire Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Enter the expected purchase price of your home and the amount you intend to contribute as a down payment.

Choose your repayment period and enter your lender's quoted annual interest rate. If you have not received a quote, consult [Freddie Mac's mortgage market survey](https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms) for a national reference.

Next, enter annual property taxes, homeowners insurance premiums and monthly association fees where applicable.

Include private mortgage insurance if required by your financing arrangement.

Review your estimated monthly housing payment and experiment with different loan terms, down payments and purchase prices.

The amortization schedule shows how much of each loan payment reduces your balance and how much goes toward interest.

Our national Mortgage Calculator also helps you compare financing arrangements outside New Hampshire.

sections.heading: How New Hampshire Property Taxes Affect Your Mortgage

blocks.markdown:
New Hampshire does not use a single statewide property tax rate for every residence. Your annual property tax liability depends on local assessments and applicable municipal, county and education tax rates.

Municipal assessors establish property values, while applicable taxing authorities determine the amounts needed to fund public services.

### Understanding property assessment and equalization

The [New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration](https://www.revenue.nh.gov/about-dra/municipal-and-property-division/property-bureau/equalization) conducts an annual equalization process with municipalities.

This process helps distribute shared property tax obligations between municipalities using comparable valuations.

Equalized municipal values should not be confused with the assessed value of an individual property shown on its tax bill.

When estimating your mortgage payment, obtain the property's actual taxable assessment and applicable local tax rate.

### New Hampshire property tax calculation example

This example excludes exemptions, credits and additional adjustments.

Two properties with identical purchase prices may have different tax bills because they are located in different municipalities.

Ask the local assessment office for current valuations, tax rates and information about upcoming revaluations.

### Property tax relief for New Hampshire homeowners

The state's [Low and Moderate Income Homeowners Property Tax Relief program](https://www.revenue.nh.gov/resource-center/taxpayer-assistance/low-and-moderate-income-homeowners-property-tax-relief) provides assistance with qualifying state education property tax expenses.

Published income limits include $37,000 for single applicants and $47,000 for married applicants or qualifying heads of household.

Ownership and residency requirements apply. Applications generally must be submitted during May or June.

Municipal exemptions and credits may also be available to eligible older homeowners, veterans and individuals with qualifying disabilities.

Do not deduct anticipated relief from your monthly mortgage estimate unless you have confirmed its eligibility, amount and payment arrangements.

Insurance premiums depend on your property's construction, condition, replacement cost, location and selected coverage.

New Hampshire properties may experience heavy snowfall, freezing temperatures, coastal storms and flooding.

Obtain property-specific insurance quotes before finalizing your purchase.

### Winter weather coverage

Ask your insurer how the policy handles frozen pipes, ice-related damage and roof damage caused by winter storms.

Older homes may have heating, plumbing or electrical systems that affect insurance eligibility or maintenance requirements.

Review coverage exclusions and deductibles carefully. Choosing a higher deductible may lower your premium but increase your financial responsibility following a covered loss.

### Flood insurance

Standard homeowners insurance generally excludes flood damage.

Properties near the coast, rivers and lakes may require separate flood coverage.

Investigate the property's location using the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home).

Include the annual premiums for all applicable insurance policies in the mortgage calculator without counting overlapping coverage twice.
The following estimates assume a 20% down payment, 6% fixed annual interest and a 30-year mortgage.

These estimates exclude property taxes, insurance, PMI and association fees.

When comparing properties, pay particular attention to local tax differences. A less expensive home in a higher-tax municipality may have similar monthly housing expenses to a more expensive property elsewhere.

New Hampshire Housing offers mortgage financing and purchase assistance through participating lenders.

### Down payment and closing cost assistance

The [New Hampshire Housing homeownership programs](https://www.nhhfa.org/homeownership/homeownership-programs/) provide eligible borrowers with assistance of up to $15,000 toward down payment and closing expenses.

Available financing arrangements include fixed assistance amounts of $5,000, $10,000 or $15,000.

Applicants should compare mortgage rates, eligibility requirements and assistance conditions before selecting a financing option.

Cash assistance should not automatically be treated as an unconditional grant. Request written information about repayment obligations and any conditions under which assistance may be forgiven.

### Preferred mortgage financing

New Hampshire Housing also offers conventional financing through its Preferred program.

Eligible borrowers with incomes below 80% of area median income may qualify for discounted mortgage insurance.

This can help reduce monthly borrowing expenses for buyers making smaller down payments.

Confirm your eligibility and compare the complete mortgage payment with other lender offers.

sections.heading: New Hampshire Real Estate Transfer Tax and Closing Costs

blocks.markdown:
Buyers should prepare for upfront expenses in addition to their down payment.

According to the [New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration](https://www.revenue.nh.gov/resource-center/frequently-asked-questions/real-estate-transfer-tax), the state's standard real estate transfer tax is $0.75 per $100 of consideration for both the buyer and seller.

On a qualifying $400,000 purchase, the buyer's standard share would be $3,000.

Other closing expenses may include mortgage origination fees, title services, inspections, appraisals and prepaid taxes or insurance.

These costs generally do not form part of your regular monthly mortgage payment unless financed through an eligible arrangement.

Review your lender's disclosures using the [CFPB Loan Estimate guide](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/loan-estimate/).

sections.heading: How Much House Can You Afford in New Hampshire?

blocks.markdown:
Begin with your reliable monthly take-home income and subtract existing household expenses.

Use our [New Hampshire Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/new-hampshire-paycheck-calculator/) to estimate after-tax earnings and our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) to evaluate borrowing obligations.

Account for winter heating, transportation, snow removal and unexpected repairs. If you commute into Massachusetts, consider transportation costs and applicable cross-border income tax obligations.

Rural properties may also involve private wells, septic systems and driveway maintenance.

Maintain enough savings to cover insurance deductibles and emergency expenses rather than spending your entire cash balance on a down payment.

### How much is a mortgage payment on a $400,000 New Hampshire home?

With 20% down, a 6% fixed interest rate and a 30-year mortgage, monthly principal and interest would be approximately $1,918.56. Property taxes, homeowners insurance and other applicable fees increase the total payment.

### How are New Hampshire property taxes calculated?

Property taxes generally depend on the property's taxable assessed value and applicable local tax rates. Municipal, county and education tax components can contribute to the final bill. Eligible exemptions or credits may reduce the amount payable.

### Does New Hampshire offer down payment assistance?

Yes. New Hampshire Housing offers qualifying borrowers assistance of up to $15,000 through eligible mortgage programs. Income, property, lending and assistance requirements apply.
